issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): The problem statement (line 94) and the template Main usage (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 32) describe and use messageOnMilk() as producing a printable textual message (String) — e.g. the problem text says: messageOnMilk() should return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" and the template calls System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()). In the solution repository, the Milkable interface declares messageOnMilk() as returning boolean (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5) and the concrete implementations (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java line 15 and solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 19) print the message inside the method and return true. This creates a direct return-type mismatch: problem + template expect a String-returning API, but the solution provides a boolean-returning API and side-effects. This will confuse students about the correct method signature and will cause compilation/test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable API consistent with the problem statement and template: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String. Update solution implementations (Seal, Goat) to return the message string (e.g. "Goat Buttinsky is milked" or "Seal Clarabelle is milked") instead of printing inside the method and returning a boolean. Alternatively, if the intended design is to perform printing inside the method, update the problem statement and template Main to reflect a void return type and not to print the returned value. Prefer changing the interface and implementations to return String to match the documented specification and template usage.
